label: 74HC163 4-bit Synchronous Binary Counter with Synchronous Clear

semantics.notes: Identical interface to 74HC161 but /CLR is SYNCHRONOUS here â€” reset only takes effect at the next rising CLK edge when /CLRN=0. This is the critical difference from 74HC161. All other behavior (ENP, ENT, /LDN, RCO, cascade) is the same. Verify that the implementation correctly defers clear to clock edge.

exportSupport.verilogNotes: always @(posedge clk) only â€” NO negedge clrn in sensitivity list (sync clear). /CLRN handled inside the always block: if (!clrn) cnt<=0;
exportSupport.vhdlNotes: process(clk) â€” clrn NOT in sensitivity list. Inside: if rising_edge then if clrn='0' then...

testability.notes: Critical test distinguishing 74HC163 from 74HC161: with /CLRN=0, apply CLKâ†‘ and verify reset happens on clock edge (NOT immediately). Verify that before CLKâ†‘, counter still holds its old value despite /CLRN=0. All other counter/load/cascade tests same as 74HC161.

risks.description: Synchronous vs asynchronous clear is the key difference from 74HC161. Must be confirmed that the implementation does NOT include clrn in async sensitivity list. High risk of copy-paste error between 161 and 163 implementations.
Verilog HDL export must NOT include 'negedge clrn' in sensitivity list. If incorrectly exports with async clear, synthesis behavior differs from simulation.
